title: Urosepsis in a DNR/COLST resident
objectives: Sepsis screen: suspected infection + >= 2 criteria -> Sepsis Alert
Read the COLST: Section A = arrest only; Sections B-D guide treatment
NS up to 30 mL/kg to MAP >= 65, lungs reassessed q500 mL
Hold position against staff pressure; Med Direction for conflicts / no response
Paramedic intercept requested without delaying transport
resources: Monitor w/ capno, O2, IV/IO kit, NS 2 x 1 L, CPAP, glucometer, thermometer, stretcher. Facility ~8 min from UVMMC.
dispatch: UVM Rescue, respond to Lakeview Terrace Health and Rehab, 450 Dorset St, South Burlington, room 214, for an 86-year-old female, altered, low blood pressure. Caller is the night nurse. Time out 0342.

scene.location: Long-term care facility, 2nd floor room, elevator. Hallway lights dimmed. ~8 min from UVMMC.
scene.setup: Pt in bed, head up, Foley bag hanging low on rail. Night RN with face sheet, MAR and DNR/COLST copy in hand.
scene.moulage: Flushed cheeks (rouge), mottling on knees (purple marker lace), warm compress on forehead.
scene.roles: Pt actor (lethargic, mumbles); night RN (pressure: "she's a DNR"); evaluator plays daughter by phone + MD.

patient.name: Dorothy Gagnon
patient.cc: More sleepy, fever, low BP on facility check
patient.on_arrival: Lying in bed, eyes closed, opens to voice, mumbles, picks at sheet. Flushed face, breathing fast.

SAMPLE: Sleepier since dinner, fever, ate 25% of dinner
Furosemide 20 mg, metoprolol 25 mg, donepezil, ASA 81 mg
Dementia (baseline A&Ox2, chatty, walker), **CHF EF 45%**, neurogenic bladder w/ **chronic Foley**, HTN
2200 T 100.4 F, cloudy urine. 0330 BP 80s, "won't wake up right"
OPQRST: Worse over 10 hr. Foley changed 9 days ago

primary: Radial **weak, rapid**. Warm flushed trunk, **mottled knees**, cap refill 4 s
GCS 12 (E3 V4 M5), baseline 14 per RN. **New AMS**
**Hot**. Foley: cloudy, foul urine. Sacrum red, intact
**HIGH**: septic shock, urinary source. COLST must be read, not assumed
secondary: Hot, flushed trunk; **mottled knees**; no wounds

vitals.other: MAP 57. Mottled knees, CRT 4 s. Lungs clear. Sinus tach

vitals.trigger: First 500 mL NS in, O2 NC 2 L

vitals.other: MAP 68. CRT 3 s. Lungs clear. Says "where am I?"
**New crackles both bases**, more work of breathing

vitals.trigger: IF no IV fluids by T+12 ("DNR")
vitals.other: MAP 49. Mottled to thighs, moans only

vitals.trigger: ~1.5 L in, en route q5 min

vitals_note: Give a value only when obtained. Bold = abnormal. 30 mL/kg = ~1.5 L.

flow.give: RN: "Dot's a DNR. The family doesn't want anything done - just take her, no needles." Hands COLST + face sheet. Stage **A** as obtained.
Show **DNR/COLST** card when crew reads it.

branches.if: Crew reads Sections B-D aloud to RN
branches.then: RN: "Oh. I thought DNR meant comfort only." Fluids, O2, CPAP, transfer allowed

expected: B-D reviewed: DNI; IV fluids + transfer OK

flow.give: IV L AC 20g on 1st attempt. Stage **B** after 500 mL.

branches.then: IO (6.4) or load and try en route; don't delay
debrief; examiner option D more likely

expected.text: NS rapid, reassess lungs q500 mL

flow.give: RN: "Our on-call NP hasn't called back. Can you wait 10 minutes?" Stage **C** at ~1 L.

branches.if: Crew waits on scene for NP or intercept

expected: COLST copy + face sheet go with pt

expected.text: Intercept meets en route, not on scene

branches.if: Daughter (HCA) by phone: "Do everything, intubate her!"
branches.then: expect calm explanation (COLST B = DNI, her consent), Med Direction; MD: "Honor the COLST; continue limited treatment."

branches.if: New crackles both bases at ~1500 mL
branches.then: Stage **D**; expect stop fluids, sit up, O2 up, CPAP (5.4) allowed by COLST C, MD re: pressors (intercept)

expected.text: Med Direction for conflict / no response

expected: Report: sepsis criteria, source, fluid total, MAP

critical: DNR read as "do not treat"; indicated fluids/O2 withheld (8.7)
COLST validity (pt identity, signature) or Sections B-D not checked (8.7)
Sepsis not recognized / no Sepsis Alert (2.23A)
No IV/IO fluid bolus with SBP <90 / MAP <65 (2.23A)
Lungs not reassessed between 500 mL boluses (2.23A)
Transport delayed for IV, intercept or facility callback
Ventilation/airway escalation against COLST Section B without MD
differentials: Chronic Foley, cloudy foul urine, fever, HR 122, MAP 57, EtCO2 21, new AMS
Warm flushed, clear lungs, no JVD
debrief: What does Section A of the COLST cover - and what doesn't it?
Which sepsis criteria did she meet, and what was the source?
Why reassess lungs every 500 mL in this patient?
How did you handle the RN and the daughter? When did you call MD?
What would have changed if Section C said comfort-focused only?

crew_card.dispatch: Lakeview Terrace Health & Rehab, 450 Dorset St, room 214. 86 y/o F, altered, low BP. Caller: night nurse.
crew_card.on_arrival: Elderly woman in bed, eyes closed, flushed, breathing fast. Urine bag on bed rail. Nurse waiting with paperwork.

actor_card.Act: Eyes closed, open to voice. Mumble, pick at sheet. Grimace when lower belly pressed.
actor_card.Orientation: Know your name only. "Is it Tuesday?"
actor_card.After ~1 L fluid: A bit brighter: "Where am I? Where's my walker?"
actor_card.Night RN: Open with "She's a DNR, no needles." Back down when crew shows Sections B-D. Ask crew to wait for NP callback at ~T+10.
actor_card.Daughter (phone): Only on examiner inject: "Do everything, put her on a breathing machine!" Calm down if crew explains the form you signed.

show_cards.title: VERMONT DNR/COLST (copy) - simulated excerpt
show_cards.body:
Patient: **Dorothy Gagnon**   DOB 02/11/1940
**A. CPR:**  [X] DNR - Do Not Attempt Resuscitation
**B. Intubation:**  [X] DNI - Do Not Intubate
**C. Other treatment:**
   [ ] Comfort-focused only
   [X] **Limited**: IV fluids, monitor, O2, noninvasive airway support (CPAP/BiPAP), transfer to hospital; no ICU
   [ ] Full treatment
**D. Antibiotics:** [X] Yes    **IV hydration:** [X] Trial    **Feeding tube:** [X] No
Consent: Linda Gagnon (daughter, health care agent)
Clinician: Sarah Morrow, APRN - signed 03/14/2026
